identity.title: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents

problem.claim: How to consolidate fragmented agent training data into unified pipelines for large-scale supervised fine-tuning.

gap.claim: Existing agent-data resources are fragmented across heterogeneous formats, tools, and interfaces, limiting standardized training; public large-scale supervised-fine-tuning results remain relatively rare.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Agent Data Protocol (ADP), a lightweight representation language acting as an interlingua between heterogeneous agent datasets and downstream training pipelines.

Defines a representation intended to cover API and tool use, browsing, coding, software engineering, and general agentic workflows while remaining simple to parse and train on without per-dataset engineering.
Unifies 13 existing agent training datasets in ADP and converts the standardized data into training-ready formats for multiple agent frameworks; code and data are publicly released.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present ADP as a unified interlingua for diverse agent datasets and training pipelines, designed to combine broad task coverage with lightweight processing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report unifying 13 existing agent training datasets into ADP and converting them for multiple agent frameworks.
The authors report approximately 20% average performance gains over corresponding base models after supervised fine-tuning on the unified data.
The authors report state-of-the-art or near-state-of-the-art results on standard coding, browsing, tool-use, and research benchmarks without domain-specific tuning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large-scale supervised fine-tuning of agents is relatively uncommon because collecting suitable training data is difficult.
The authors attribute the bottleneck primarily to fragmentation across data formats, tools, and interfaces rather than a shortage of underlying sources.
ADP is introduced as a lightweight interlingua connecting diverse datasets to unified downstream training pipelines.
The authors standardize 13 datasets, prepare them for multiple frameworks, and report gains and strong benchmark performance without domain-specific tuning.
Code and data are publicly released to support standardized, scalable, and reproducible agent training.

source_observation.claim: The abstract diagnoses dataset fragmentation and then links the proposed representation to heterogeneous task coverage and multiple downstream frameworks.

lessons.interpretation: A concrete bottleneck-to-interface mapping can make a systems contribution's purpose and scope easier to assess.
lessons.application: When proposing a data or infrastructure layer, explicitly map the diagnosed incompatibilities to supported task types, conversion targets, and downstream consumers.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the main contribution is a single-task algorithm whose value does not depend on interoperability.

unknowns: The abstract does not define how the approximately 20% average gain is aggregated, which metrics or splits are used, or how corresponding base models are selected.
Details of the benchmark baselines, statistical variation, dataset composition, and conversion fidelity are not provided, so the reported comparisons cannot be independently assessed here.
